title: Introduce 'Signal Weave' dashboard and invocation-stitch metrics for cohort-based alerting
author: Asha Menon
description: Context: Production alert noise and incident response frequently require stitching metric spikes to related trace fragments to surface causal token-phase regressions. Motivation: Provide a compact, actionable observability surface that correlates trace edges with token-phase metrics and lets SREs tune alerts per invocation cohort. What this PR does: 1) Adds a new dashboard 'Signal Weave' that combines short-window metric rollups (per-token phase CPU/latency/cost) with trace-stitch visualizations including span-edge heatmap and a compact invocation timeline; 2) Introduces invocation_stitch_collector, a lightweight collector that emits invocation-edge anchors (span IDs + token-phase fingerprints) and a small token-phase summary to the metrics pipeline; 3) Adds cohort_policy.go which implements cohort-aware alert thresholds and a simple dampening hysteresis to reduce noisy flapping for low-volume tenants; 4) Adds SQL and dashboard queries to compute cohort percentiles and a sparkline that surfaces cost-latency drift; 5) Exposes a per-tenant rollout manifest and feature flag that will gate collector activation. Design notes: Collector is intentionally CPU-light and rate-limited with backpressure; it batches anchors and emits a compact fingerprint (md5-like human-safe hex) to avoid PII leak and keeps token counts only as aggregated histograms. The dashboard uses compact sparklines and a stitched-trace panel that requests sample spans via the existing trace API. Rollout plan: gate behind feature flag; 10% tenants for week 1, 50% week 2, full rollout week 4 pending no regressions. Backwards compatibility: collector defaults to off; no schema migration for long-term storage. Testing: unit tests for cohort_policy and collector logic, e2e dashboard snapshot test, perf smoke that validates collector CPU < 1 core at 1k invocations/sec in our staging harness. Related work: complements ENG-3712 (token-phase metrics), builds on ENG-3608 (trace sampling v2).
